content:
Division in Class 3 introduces the quotient, the remainder and long-division thinking. This guide explains what the IMO Class 3 division chapter tests, the facts to know, the traps, and a free 10-question online test with answers.

What the Class 3 Maths Olympiad Division chapter tests

  • Division facts and fact families
  • Division of 2- and 3-digit numbers by a 1-digit number
  • Quotient and remainder
  • Word problems

Key facts your child should know

  • Dividend = Quotient × Divisor + Remainder, and the remainder is always less than the divisor.
  • Division undoes multiplication: 6 × 4 = 24 → 24 ÷ 6 = 4.
  • Any number ÷ 1 = itself; a number ÷ itself = 1.
  • 0 ÷ any number = 0; you cannot divide by 0.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Leaving a remainder that is bigger than the divisor.
  • Forgetting the fact-family link with multiplication.
  • Miscounting during long division.

quiz.title: IMO Class 3 Division Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: In the division 70 ÷ 8 = 8 remainder 6, which number is the divisor?
questions.explanation: The divisor is the number we divide BY. Here 70 (dividend) ÷ 8 (divisor) = 8 (quotient), remainder 6.

questions.q: 63 apples are shared equally among 7 baskets. How many does each basket holds?
questions.explanation: Divide the total by the number of baskets: 63 ÷ 7 = 9.

questions.q: When 52 is divided by 6, what is the remainder?
In the division 38 ÷ 4 = 9 remainder 2, which number is the divisor?
questions.explanation: The divisor is the number we divide BY. Here 38 (dividend) ÷ 4 (divisor) = 9 (quotient), remainder 2.

questions.q: 137 nuts are shared equally among 4 children. How many nuts does each child get, and how many are left over?
questions.explanation: 137 ÷ 4 = 34 remainder 1. Each child gets 34 nuts, and 1 are left over.

questions.q: Which of these divisions by 9 leaves NO remainder?
questions.explanation: 36 = 9 × 4, so 36 ÷ 9 = 4 exactly; the others leave remainders.

faq.a: The amount left over when a number does not divide exactly. 23 ÷ 5 = 4 remainder 3, because 4 × 5 + 3 = 23.
Multiply the quotient by the divisor and add the remainder — it should equal the dividend.
